questions.q: What is the passage's main argument?
options: Genius is an inborn gift that no amount of effort can replace
Great results come mainly from ordinary qualities like diligence
Fortune decides who succeeds regardless of how hard they work
Only mastery of a single subject brings lasting recognition
questions.explain: It says the greatest results come from simple means and ordinary qualities such as application and perseverance.

options: The power of lighting one's own fire
Common sense intensified
Patience
The power of making efforts
questions.explain: Buffon said of genius 'it is patience.'

questions.q: How did Newton say he made his discoveries?
options: By waiting for inspiration to strike
By always thinking unto them
By consulting other philosophers
By experiments conducted at night
questions.explain: Asked by what means, Newton answered 'By always thinking unto them.'

questions.q: How did Peel's father train his boyhood memory?
options: He made him copy out long books by hand each week
He had him study Latin at dawn before breakfast
He had him recite poetry to guests every evening
He had him repeat the Sunday sermon from memory
questions.explain: His father had him practise speaking extempore and repeat the Sunday sermon, until he could do so almost verbatim.

questions.q: What would the author say about whether labour alone could produce a Shakespeare or Newton?
options: It could, given enough years of patient daily practice
It could not, as original talent of heart and brain is needed
It could, if the person lived a simple and orderly life
It is impossible to say without knowing their early training
questions.explain: He grants labour's achievements but says no amount of it could produce such figures without the original endowment.
